result:
The final answer 1/18 is plausible, but I could not fully verify that it is the sharp constant.

**Lower bound (the construction) checks out.** Take three parts $V_1,V_2,V_3$ of size $n/3$. Use a $K_4$-free Bollobás–Erdős graph of density $1/2$ between each pair of parts, with sparse triangle-free graphs inside each part. Any $K_5$ must place at least 4 vertices in some union of two parts (since the three pairwise unions have total size $10$, one has size at least $4$). That union induces a $K_4$-free graph, so no $K_5$ exists. The independence number is $o(n)$.

For a bipartition, let $x_i$ be the fraction of $V_i$ on side $A$. The forced deletions are about
$$\tfrac12\left(\tfrac n3\right)^2\sum_{i<j}\big(x_ix_j+(1-x_i)(1-x_j)\big).$$
This sum is bilinear in $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$, so its minimum over $[0,1]^3$ is attained at a vertex of the cube. Checking the eight vertices, the minimum is $1$, attained when exactly one or two of the $x_i$ equal 1. So the construction forces $\frac{n^2}{18}+o(n^2)$ deletions.

**Upper bound not verified.** The problem asks for the smallest $c$ that works for every graph, so one would also need a matching upper bound. I checked a few other natural constructions. A blow-up of $C_5$ with density-$1/2$ pairs is $K_5$-free but needs only about $n^2/50$ deletions. I did not establish that no weighted construction forces more than $n^2/18$. This is consistent with $1/18$ being the known sharp value, but I could not confirm it from the literature.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
